caseno:
Second Appeal No. 306 of 1976 
and 
Second Appeal No. 307 of 1976.
lawyer:
Miah Abdul Gafur with NK Saha and Abbasuddin Ahmed, Advocates ----- For the Appellant
Nurul Hoque with AKM Shahidul Huq and Tania Siddique, Advocates ----- For the Respondent
parties:
Santosh Kumar Paul ------ Appellant
vs 
Nuruddin Ansari ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 15. Mr. Md. Abdul Gafur, the learned Advocate for the appellant Santosh Kumar Paul, has firstly taken me through both the impugned judgments of the courts below and thereafter he argues that the impugned judgment of the Court of appeal below are not at all proper judgments of reversal and the learned Additional District Judge without sufficiently adverting to the reasonings of the trial Court reversed the findings and decisions of the said court and held that the Bainanama Ext. B. was a genuine document of agreement executed by the defendant appellant and accordingly, he allowed both the appeals on contest with cost and set aside the impugned judgments and decree of the trial Court and thereafter decreed Title Suit No. 108 of 1974 on contest with costs against the contesting defendant and ex parte against defendant No.2 and dismissed Title Suit No. 221 of 1973 on contest with costs against the contesting defendant and ex parte against defendant No. 2 and thus allowed the specific performance of contract subject to payment of the balance consideration money of Taka 300.00 to defendant Santosh Kumar Paul by the plaintiff Nuruddin Ansari. The learned Advocate for the appellant argued that the trial Court correctly considered the evidence on record and observed that the date in the schedule of land in the Bainapatra Ext. B appeared to have been inserted later on though the signature of the executant Santosh Kumar Paul in the said Bainapatra appeared to be genuine in spite of the fact that the signature of plaintiff Santosh Kumar Paul of the 1st suit was found to be with a different ink, The trial Court however expressed doubt as to the genuineness of the Bainapatra Ext. B. and hence the learned Munsif was pleased to decree the suit being TS No. 221 of 1973 in part subject to payment of the sum of Taka 901.00 to the contesting defendant Nuruddin Ansari by the plaintiff Santosh Kumar. Accordingly the other suit being TS No. 108 of 1974 was decreed in part. Now, it is the contention of the learned Advocate for the appellant that the lower appellant Court has not properly considered the evidence on record and wrongly found that the Bainapatra Ext. B was a genuine document and the same was voluntarily executed by the defendant Santosh Kumar Paul and accordingly decreed in full the suit being TS No. 108/1974 of the present plaintiff respondent for specific performance of contract subject to payment of the balance amount of Taka 300.00 to the contesting defendant Santosh Kumar Paul who was also directed to execute and register the necessary kabala deed within 30 days from date of receipt of notice of the deposit of the above balance consideration money in court by the plaintiff, in default the plaintiff i.e. the present respondent Nuruddin Ansari be free to get the kabala deed executed and registered through the court in his favour. The learned Advocate for the appellant has drawn my attention to the impugned Bainapatra Ext. B and tried to show that there were some gaps here and there in some parts of the same and also absence of some figures of the consideration money and writings of the date, and the figures therein and that the Bainapatra appears to have been written by the contesting defendant with a different ink showing subsequent writings. The learned Advocate for the appellant therefore, contends that the learned Additional District Judge without noticing the above defects in the alleged Bainapatra (Ext. 1) B. wrongly believed the case of the plaintiff Nuruddin Ansari and found the Bainapatra Ext. B to have been genuinely executed by the contesting defendant Santosh Kumar Paul, on receipt of some earnest money from the plaintiff Nuruddin and illegally found the Bainapatra (Ext. B) as genuine one and wrongly decreed the suit for specific performance of contract subject to payment of the remaining consideration money and illegally dismissed the suit of the appellant Santosh Kumar Paul i.e. Title Suit No. 221/1973. It is further contended by the learned Advocate for the appellant that the learned court of appeal below failed to see that the signature of the defendant Santosh Kumar Paul appearing in the Bainapatra Ext. B. might be genuine but the same was obtained through undue influence and intimidation and, as such, the said Bainapatra ought to to have been held to be not genuine and the suit of the respondent Nuruddin Ansari ought to have been dismissed. In reply to the above submissions of the learned Advocate for the appellants, Mr. Nurul Haque, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondent however argued that the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the appellant relates mainly to the question of facts as to whether the Bainapatra was genuine or not. He further submits that the allegations made by the learned Advocate for the appellant that the dates, days, years and some figures of the schedule of lands were introduced on different dates by a different hand and different ink are not correct. The learned Additional District Judge, on scrutiny of the said document Ext. B. the figures, dates and other writings therein along with the evidence on record came to the findings that the defendant Santosh Kumar Paul voluntarily executed the Bainapatra (Ext. B) by putting his signature on receipt of the earnest money and the same was a genuine one. The learned Advocate for the respondent further contends that this court of Second Appeal is bound by the finding of fact of the court of appeal below if such finding of course is not a perverse one. He further contends that this court in Second Appeal cannot go to disturb any finding of fact if arrived at on due consideration of the evidence on record. In this connection he has referred to section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure and relied on a decision in the case of Abdul Mannaf Khan and others vs. Bangladesh and another reported in 38 DLR (AD) 201 wherein it been observed "As far back as 1880 AD in the case of Durga Choudin vs. Jawher Singh 17 Indian Appeal 122 (PC) the Privy Council emphatically declared under section 584 of the earlier Code which corresponds to section 100 of the present Code, there is no jurisdiction to entertain a second appeal on the ground of erroneous finding of fact, however gross or inexcusable the error may seem to be; and they added a note of warning, that no court in India has power to add or enlarge the grounds specified in section 100. The learned Advocate for the respondent therefore contends that both the courts below found the signature of the executant Santosh Kumar Paul in the Bainapatra Ext. B to be voluntary and genuine on his acceptance of the earnest money of Taka 901.00 from Nuruddin Ansari. Hence the basic facts for the proof of genuineness of the agreement i.e. Bainapatra Ext. B have been concurrently found to be proved by both the courts below and ultimately Ext. B, has been found to be genuine, hence there was no scope for interference by this court in second appeal in the above concurrent finding of facts of the court below. Of course as to the voluntariness of the execution of the said Ext. B, the trial Court appears to have expressed some doubt but in the long run it did not come to any specific finding to the effect that the agreement Ext. B. was false or fraudulent due to subsequent writing of date or figures by any different ink in the agreement. However this aspect of the matter has been thoroughly scrutinised and considered by the lower appellate Court vis-a-vis the evidence on record and ultimately, it came to a conclusive finding that the said Bainapatra was written in the same sitting as per instructions of the executant Santosh Kumar Paul on receipt of the earnest money of Rs. 901.00 and hence Ext. B was a genuine contract for sale of the suit-land of the executant Santosh Kumar Paul.
